title: Chicago sidemen, Armstrong and Bechet
summary: He recalls Sugar Johnny, Mutt Carey, King Oliver and Armstrong joining him, praises Armstrong, and admires Bechet.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: That was the only band. That's the only colored band in history to play a World Series of the country.
Mr. Dewey, would you tell us some of the fine players that played with you or that you knew while you were in Chicago?

Well, I left New Orleans with Sugar Johnny, and he got in bad health, and I switched to Mud Carry. After Mud Carry, the climate was too cold. He dropped me in Chicago, came back to New Orleans and sent King Oliver with me. So King Oliver stuck with me a while later, then he sent Armstrong later. Mr. Dewey, what did you think about Armstrong? I mean, as much as you know about him, what do you think about him? Greatest. One in the world greatest. Do you like his style of playing? Oh, yes. I really do. Did he play any different style from what they have played in New Orleans? New Orleans style? Oh, yes. Was jazz changing at that point? Was it changing to a, in a different, was it a different form, or was it still the same old Dixieland? The same, the same old Dixieland, but Armstrong added a little more to it. Now, Mr. Dewey, about the musicians in Chicago, did they come down and listen to you and learn jazz in that way? Is that the way they learned jazz? From one orchestra to another in New Orleans, they made all those nightclubs to be sure that when they'd go back they'd have an idea of what jazz was. In other words, they learned, they came down to New Orleans to find out about it. They didn't wait until you got to Chicago. No, indeed not. Mr. Dewey, did you have anybody especially that you admired as a player on your own instrument, like a clarinet player? Oh, yes. I admire Sidney Bershaw. In fact, he was with me and we fell out on that account because I read and he didn't read but he could outplay me.
